extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys, drug sponsors, and any interested persons (e.g., generic manufacturers) involved in FDA patent-term-extension procedures
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive criteria FDA uses to determine a product's regulatory review period for purposes of patent-term extension, plus instructions for submitting comments and petitions challenging dates or diligence. Applies to human drug product (NDA) patent-extension proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory review period composition
rubrics_metrics.description: A regulatory review period consists of two periods of time: a testing phase and an approval phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For human drug products, the testing phase begins when the exemption to permit the clinical investigations of the drug becomes effective and runs until the approval phase begins. The approval phase starts with the initial submission of an application to market the human drug product and continues until FDA grants permission to market the drug product. FDA's determination of the length of a regulatory review period for a human drug product will include all of the testing phase and approval phase as specified in 35 U.S.C. 156(g)(1)(B).

rubrics_metrics.name: Testing phase start date (IND effective date)
rubrics_metrics.description: The testing phase begins when the exemption under section 505(i) of the FD&C Act (21 U.S.C. 355(i)) became effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may claim a particular IND effective date, but FDA will verify and rely on its records (e.g., an IND effective date may be 30 days after FDA receipt of the IND). The notice gives an example where the applicant claimed November 23, 2016, but FDA records indicated September 26, 2015 (30 days after receipt).

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval phase start date (initial application submission)
rubrics_metrics.description: The approval phase starts with the initial submission of an application to market the human drug product under section 505 of the FD&C Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FDA verifies the applicant's claimed initial submission date (example: FDA verified that NDA 217369 was initially submitted on December 5, 2022). The approval phase continues until FDA approval (permission to market) is granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination establishes maximum potential extension; USPTO statutory limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA's determination of the regulatory review period establishes the maximum potential length of a patent extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO applies statutory limitations in calculating the actual extension (for example, half the testing phase must be subtracted and any time that occurred before the patent was issued may be excluded). Thus FDA's measured regulatory-review-period length may be reduced by USPTO statutory calculations when awarding actual patent-term extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation and verification of component dates (including other regulatory actions)
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA will derive the lengths of testing and approval phases from verifiable dates such as IND effective date, initial NDA submission date, and other controlling regulatory actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice lists and verifies the dates used (e.g., IND effective date, NDA submission date, date of issuance of interim final rule controlling the drug under 21 U.S.C. 811 (Controlled Substances Act) section 201(j)). Other regulatory actions (e.g., DEA scheduling or interim final rules) may be relevant to the timeline and are included where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment submission requirements and responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Anyone with knowledge that any of the dates as published are incorrect may submit electronic or written comments and ask for a redetermination by the stated deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic comments are submitted via https://www.regulations.gov and will be posted to the docket unchanged; commenters are solely responsible for ensuring comments do not include confidential information (e.g., medical information, SSNs, confidential business information). Late/untimely filed comments will not be considered. Written/paper submissions must include the docket numbers and will be considered timely only if received by the closing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential submissions procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure for submitting comments with confidential information that you do not wish to be made publicly available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit confidential comments only as written/paper submissions and provide two copies: (1) one copy containing the information claimed confidential with a heading or cover note stating 'THIS DOCUMENT CONTAINS CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION' (the Agency will review this copy), and (2) a redacted/blacked-out copy that will be available for public viewing and posted on regulations.gov. Submit both copies to Dockets Management Staff. Information marked 'confidential' will not be disclosed except in accordance with 21 CFR 10.20 and other applicable law. If you do not wish your name/contact information made public, provide it on the cover sheet and not in the body of your comments and identify it as 'confidential.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency posting, review, and redaction policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies review all submissions and may choose to redact or withhold certain submissions (or portions thereof); submitted comments may not be available to be read until the agency has approved them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments submitted electronically, including attachments, to regulations.gov will be posted unchanged. However, the agency may withhold or redact submissions. For more information about FDA's posting of comments to public dockets, see 80 FR 56469 (Sept. 18, 2015).

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitions for redetermination and due diligence (21 CFR 60.24 and 60.30) — content and procedural requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 21 CFR 60.24, anyone may ask for a redetermination of published dates; under 21 CFR 60.30 any interested person may petition FDA to determine whether the applicant for extension acted with due diligence during the regulatory review period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To meet its burden, a petition must comply with all requirements of §60.30, including but not limited to: must be timely (see DATES), must be filed in accordance with 21 CFR 10.20, must contain sufficient facts to merit an FDA investigation, and must certify that a true and complete copy of the petition has been served upon the patent applicant. Petitions should be in the format specified in 21 CFR 10.30. Example deadlines given: requests for redetermination by March 9, 2026; petitions regarding due diligence by July 6, 2026. Submit petitions electronically at regulations.gov (specified docket) or send two copies for written petitions to the Dockets Management Staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Docket access and identification requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructions for accessing the docket and identifying submissions correctly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To access the docket and view background documents or comments, go to https://www.regulations.gov and insert the docket number (found in brackets in the heading) into the 'Search' box. All submissions must include the docket numbers FDA-2024-E-1294; FDA-2024-E-1295; FDA-2024-E-1296; and FDA-2024-E-1297 for this matter. Written/paper submissions are available for public viewing at the Dockets Management Staff between 9 a.m. and 4 p.m., Monday through Friday, phone 240-402-7500.
